messages:
ben.j: Observed a weird quality regression after enabling the new FP8 kernels on L40S for model x-phi-13b. Short prompts fine, but >1024 tokens we see hallucination spikes and sudden token collapse around step ~1200.

miguel: Can you paste the smallest repro? config + a couple of examples?

ben.j: Pasting a trimmed log and canary config. Note the strange activation clipping warnings from the runtime.

ben.j: ```
cmd: ./serve --model x-phi-13b --quant fp8 --device l40s --tiles 256
log: [runtime] activation_clip: layer=9 mean=0.002 std=0.47 clip_ratio=0.83
log: [runtime] kv_cache_miss: seq=1302 drop=1 fallback=int8
metrics: p50_latency=62ms p95=95ms tokens/s=420
quality: ppl=12.3 -> 17.8 (on long-prompt eval set)
```

tara: Hmm those clip_ratio numbers are high. Could be per-layer scale overflow when sequence grows. Did you enable per-layer autotune?

ben.j: No autotune yet — we rolled FP8 on canary 10% with default scale calibration. Also saw more NaNs in attention scores in the same windows.

sophie: Is this H100-only pattern or L40S-specific? We had similar issues last month but on H100 it was stable after bias-correction patch.

ben.j: On H100 with same config it was okay. L40S seems more sensitive to tiling/packing differences (we use 32x8 tiling).

miguel: Two quick hypotheses: 1) activation range estimation underestimates tail values for long sequences, so FP8 saturates mid-run; 2) KV cache alignment/tiling mismatch causes effective attention scaling to change. Both could make logits explode/vanish.

eva: Can we repro with AWQ/GPTQ for the same sequences to see if quant algorithm matters? If AWQ keeps the dynamic range better, that points to quantization calibration.

ben.j: Ran a mini-bakeoff this morning:
- FP8 runtime kernel (current) -> ppl long=17.8, tokens/s=420
- AWQ 4-bit -> ppl long=13.5, tokens/s=380
- GPTQ 4-bit -> ppl long=14.1, tokens/s=360
- INT8 fallback (select layers 8-12) -> ppl long=12.6, tokens/s=410
So FP8 fastest but worst quality on long prompts.

tara: Interesting that INT8 mixed gives best ppl. Suggests a small subset of layers (maybe mid-transformer) are responsible. Can we run per-layer sensitivity by freezing FP8->INT8 one layer at a time?

ben.j: Yup started that: layer 8 and 9 fixes most of the drift. When 8/9 forced to INT8, ppl drops to 12.8 and no clip warnings. tokens/s=405.

sophie: That aligns with activation-wide trend: mid layers have larger dynamic ranges for long-horizon context. Parking a rule in runtime: "fp8-exempt-layers" that fallback automatically for layers scoring clip_ratio>0.6.

runtime-bot: Suggestion: create canary route with env FP8_AUTO_FALLBACK=true and FP8_FALLBACK_THRESH=0.6. Monitor `activation_clip` metric. Auto-disable after 5 consecutive clips.

miguel: Runbook proposal:
1) repro with deterministic seed and long-prompt eval suite (we have ~200 prompts).
2) confirm layer-level clip_ratio histogram.
3) try per-layer bayesian scale calibrator (freeze/shift) and re-run AWQ vs FP8.
4) if persistent, create kernel patch to clamp pre-attention scale normalization for L40S tiling.

eva: Also check KV cache packing alignment on L40S: small pointer/stride differences can change summation order and thus FP8 rounding noise accumulation over long sequences. Add a comparison of kv checksums between H100/L40S.

ben.j: Good call — I'll add kv checksums. Quick note: using FAST_KV_SPLIT=true reduced clip events by ~30% but didn't eliminate regressions.

tara: Can we do an intermediate canary: 10% traffic to route A (FP8 default), 40% to B (FP8 with auto-fallback layers 8-10), 50% INT8-mixed baseline. Observe log-loss and latency for 24h.

ben.j: Will spin up the canary after I get the checksum probe in. ETA ~3h.

sophie: If canary shows it's layer-local, we should make per-model default exemptions in model catalog (metadata: fp8_exempt_layers). Avoid global kernel toggles.

miguel: For longer-term: consider a tiny per-sequence calibration step for FP8 that warms per-layer scales using the first 128 tokens (cheap, async). Might recover quality for long prompts with minimal perf hit.

eva: Also record golden outputs (sha256) for a small set to detect bit-exact drift during kernel upgrades. We had false negatives when metrics looked ok but outputs diverged.

ben.j: Thanks — I'll post back with canary results and kv checksums. For now, disabling global FP8 rollout until we have auto-fallback and layer exemptions in place. :raised_hands:

tara: Thanks team. Keep thread updated. If we need a hotfix for L40S kernel, flag eng-runtime and eng-infra oncall.
